title: One bounded loop iteration
statement: Let a program, depth bound, condition $c$, body statement $s$, initial state $\sigma$, time bounds $T_1,T_2,T\in\mathbb N$, and postcondition $Q$ be given. If $c$ is safe and true at $\sigma$, and the body can execute from $\sigma$ within time $T_1$ to a state from which the same loop can end in a state satisfying $Q$ within time $T_2$, and $\operatorname{cost}(c)+1+T_1+T_2\le T$, then the loop ends from $\sigma$ in a state satisfying $Q$ within time $T$.
hypotheses_covered: The condition is safe at the initial state
The condition holds at the initial state
The body reaches within $T_1$ a state from which the loop reaches a $Q$-state within $T_2$
The combined time bound is at most $T$
